rationale:
ROUND 3. Round 2 was 8 approve / 2 object. Both objections were correct, both are FIXED IN CODE, and one of them led me to a worse defect than the one reported.

(A) editquality [MEDIUM] — 'navLabelDropCategoryPrefix returns the ORIGINAL label (slash intact) when the tail after the last / is empty; the invariant is not guaranteed, only the common case; no test exercises this branch'. CORRECT, and fixed. The function now scans backwards for the last segment WITH CONTENT, which cannot return a separator. An all-separator label names no page, so it falls through to the title rather than returning separators or empty. Five new test cases pin it (trailing-sep, trailing-sep-nospace, leading-sep, only-seps, only-seps-spaced).

(B) THE DEFECT THAT OBJECTION (A) UNCOVERED, which is worse than (A) and which no seat reported: splitting on ANY '/' mangles the perfectly good label 'A/B Test Calculator' into 'B Test Calculator'. I found it writing the test for (A), by checking whether any real title or label contains a slash instead of assuming none did. webdesign.co.uk has a page named tool-ab-test-calculator titled 'A/B Test Calculator | webdesign.co.uk' — the ONE title in the fleet containing a slash. It has no authored nav_label today, so the mangling was LATENT rather than live, which is the kind that ships. The rule is now narrowed: only a WHITESPACE-DELIMITED slash is a category separator; an intra-word slash is part of the name. All 8 live slash-bearing nav_labels use the 'Tools / X' form, so the narrower rule still fixes every real case, and it also answers the guardian's round-2 low objection about co-equal slashes for the intra-word half.
This also corrected the TEST'S OWN ASSERTION, which was too strong and would have condemned 'A/B Test Calculator': it now requires that no category SEPARATOR survive, not that no slash survive.

(C) prior_art_librarian [HIGH] — 'the landmine as it reads in the council's OWN roster is still the unqualified absolute with no NARROWED marker; that is the shape of a false register-correction claim, asserted-fixed not verified'. THIS WAS A CORRECT CATCH AND MY CLAIM WAS FALSE AS STATED. The cause: I ran scripts/landmines-sync.py --apply at ~18:24, then edited LANDMINES.md at ~18:35, and never re-synced — so the file was fixed and the doc_notes roster the council actually reads was not. Repo and roster had diverged, and I asserted the roster state from the file. Re-synced (490 owned rows across 111 entries) and VERIFIED BY READING THE ROSTER BACK rather than by reading the file: the doc_notes row now returns has_status_first=t, has_narrowed=t, and the correction appears within the first 200 characters, so it survives the truncation that hid it from four seats in round 1. Logged in WRONG_CALLS.md: a doc edit is not a delivered correction until the store the reader queries has it, and 'I fixed it at source' is a claim about a PIPELINE, not a file.

(D) prior_art_librarian [MEDIUM] — 'the 4486f1a9 precedent is cited as settled fact but not checked against diagnosis_artifacts; if it does not exist or reached a different verdict the whole narrative collapses'. Checked, from the artifact rather than from memory: decision 'approved', decided_by 'approved with 2 advisory objection(s) — none high-severity', 12 reviewers, 5 abstained, objection severities {medium: 2, low: 9}, zero high. Exactly as cited.

(E) prior_art_librarian [LOW] — 'deadness is reasserted via git at HEAD, which this council's code_checks tier cannot corroborate; log it as an author-supplied claim, not settled'. Accepted as stated, and logged as such: it is an author-supplied claim, verifiable only outside this council's tooling, and it is recorded that way in bugs_open/149 A7 with the exact commands so the next reader re-runs rather than inherits it. It is also why A7 exists at all rather than the sibling being fixed on the strength of my own grep.

NOTHING ELSE CHANGED. The blast radius, the live defect, the second-site proof and the independence-from-the-delete-landmine evidence are unchanged from round 2 and carried forward below.

ORIGINAL RATIONALE, carried forward because each round is judged standalone. bugs_open/149 A6 installed the rule that a nav label never contains a path separator, and pinned it in nav_membership_test.go. That guarantee reaches every label the derivation COMPUTES (navSimplifyLabel) and stops at the function boundary beside it: navLabelForPage returns a planner-AUTHORED pages.nav_label VERBATIM whenever it is <=30 characters, slash and all. I found this while carrying out the guardian seat's round-1 request on the A6 submission — that the label fix be proven on a site other than the one-site spot check — by measuring the AUTHORED column rather than the derived one. It is not hypothetical: ai-agent-orchestration.com is currently serving an active nav row labelled 'Tools / AI Readiness Quiz'. Blast radius is measured, not asserted: 8 live pages carry a slash-shaped nav_label, 7 of them flagged for nav; 2 are short enough to be returned verbatim (one already in nav), and the other 5 are long enough that navSimplifyLabel already rewrites them from the URL. So this changes at most 7 labels fleet-wide and today fixes 1 served defect. The other consumers of the same mechanism were checked rather than assumed: the buggy older twin rerenderSimplifyNavLabel (rerender_pages_actions.go:440) still title-cases the whole path exactly as the pre-A6 code did, but is reachable only from rerenderGetHeaderNavFromDB and rerenderGetFooterNavFromDB, whose only call site is commented out at rerender_pages_actions.go:168 — dead, so it is deliberately NOT touched here rather than fixed speculatively; datahelpers.SimplifyNavLabel takes a page NAME, not a URL, so it cannot title-case a path; and getNavItemsFromPagesFallback already routes through the fixed navSimplifyLabel. This edit is therefore the single live gap. Documentation of the dead twin is attached to the register entry, not to this change. Note on the shape of the remedy: the obvious alternative — sending any slash-bearing authored label through navSimplifyLabel — is worse, because the URL fallback flattens the planner's capitalisation ('ai-readiness-quiz' becomes 'Ai Readiness Quiz', where the planner wrote 'AI Readiness Quiz'). Taking the last segment keeps the planner's words. The prefix is redundant in nav regardless of the slash: the item already sits inside a nav GROUP, so the label only has to name the page.

plan.summary: navLabelForPage trusts a planner-authored pages.nav_label verbatim when it is <=30 chars, so an authored label shaped 'Tools / AI Readiness Quiz' reaches a live nav row with its category prefix and slash intact — breaking, on the authored path, the no-slash invariant that bugs_open/149 A6 installed and tested on the derived path. Drop the category prefix from an authored label BEFORE the length test, so no slash survives and an oversized label still falls through to navSimplifyLabel.

edits.rationale: Round 3. Two corrections on top of round 2's edit, both from the council: (1) return the last segment WITH CONTENT, so an all-separator tail cannot hand back the original slash-bearing label — editquality showed the guarantee held only for the common case; (2) treat ONLY a whitespace-delimited slash as a category separator, because splitting on any '/' mangles 'A/B Test Calculator' to 'B Test Calculator', and webdesign.co.uk really has that page. An all-separator label names no page and falls through to the title. The title is deliberately NOT stripped — a nav_label is a display field with a category convention, a title is prose.

Round 3 adds the branch editquality found unexercised (degenerate separators) and the intra-word-slash case that branch uncovered, and corrects the assertion itself: it demanded no SLASH survive, which would condemn 'A/B Test Calculator'; it now demands no category SEPARATOR survive. Proven against the round-1 implementation: 5 FAILs, including navLabelForPage("Tools / ") = "Tools / " and the A/B mangling.

grounded_in: LIVE DEFECT, site_nav_items 2026-07-31: SELECT s.domain, ni.label, ng.group_type FROM site_nav_items ni JOIN site_nav_groups ng ON ng.id=ni.group_id JOIN sites s ON s.id=ni.site_id WHERE ni.status='active' AND ni.label LIKE '%/%'; => ai-agent-orchestration.com | Tools / AI Readiness Quiz | utility  (1 row)

BLAST RADIUS, measured not asserted, pages 2026-07-31: 8 rows have nav_label LIKE '%/%' and status IN ('active','deployed','pending'); 7 are flagged in_header or in_footer; exactly 2 have length(nav_label) <= 30 and are therefore returned verbatim today — 'Tools / AI Readiness Quiz' (25) and 'Tools / AI Agent ROI Estimator' (30).

THE CODE'S OWN STATED RULE, nav_tables.go:569 (added by bugs_open/149 A6): 'A label containing a slash is never right, so the derivation takes the page's own segment: the last non-empty path segment, ignoring a trailing index.'

THE BYPASS, populate_nav_tables_action.go:498-510 before this change: 'if page.NavLabel != "" { ... if len(page.NavLabel) <= 30 { return page.NavLabel } ; return navSimplifyLabel(page.NavLabel, page.URL) }' — the <=30 branch never consults navSimplifyLabel at all.

SIBLINGS CHECKED, not assumed: rerenderSimplifyNavLabel (rerender_pages_actions.go:440) still derives from the whole path ('name := strings.TrimPrefix(url, "/"); name = strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".html")'), i.e. it still contains the pre-A6 defect — but its only two callers rerenderGetHeaderNavFromDB and rerenderGetFooterNavFromDB are reached from exactly one site, which is commented out: rerender_pages_actions.go:168 '/*dbNav := rerenderGetHeaderNavFromDB(ctx, params.DB, siteID, 6, params.Logger)*/'. nav_tables.go:12 already labels the footer twin '[dead code]'.

SECOND-SITE PROOF that motivated the measurement (gaswholesalers.com, corr fd85fc84-f021-4e47-801a-db4c90174127, chassis v1.0.1218, 18:16 UTC): 19 active nav rows before, 23 after; the 4 additions all landed in utility with labels 'Fuel Cost Estimator', 'Gas Unit Converter', 'Breakeven Volume Calculator', 'Fuel Budget Forecaster'; the 19 pre-existing labels were unchanged. The page title reads 'Wholesale Break-Even Volume Calculator | Tools' while the label reads 'Breakeven Volume Calculator', so the label is provably URL-derived rather than title-derived.

GUARD PROVEN TO FAIL ON THE DEFECT (RUNBOOK R9 discipline): with 'label := navLabelDropCategoryPrefix(page.NavLabel)' reverted to 'label := page.NavLabel', go test -run TestAuthoredNavLabelNeverKeepsItsCategoryPrefix produces 4 FAILs including 'navLabelForPage(nav_label="Tools / AI Readiness Quiz") = "Tools / AI Readiness Quiz" — a nav label must never contain a path separator'; restored, the package is ok.

SHARED-TREE CHECK: git archive HEAD extracted clean, overlaid with only these two files, 'go build ./platform/...' succeeds and 'go test ./platform/orchestration/actions/' is ok — so this commit cannot break HEAD via another session's uncommitted work in the same package.

ROUND 1 GATING OBJECTION ANSWERED AT SOURCE — the landmine's own NARROWED bullet, added by this lane on 2026-07-31 before this submission existed: 'NARROWED 2026-07-31 (chassis v1.0.1215, council 4486f1a9 APPROVED) — STILL TRUE, but only for a page that declares NO nav flag. classifyPagesForNav now demotes a child-path page to the utility group instead of dropping it, provided in_header or in_footer is set — so a rebuild KEEPS such a link where it used to delete it (6 of the 7 affected rows fleet-wide).'

THE LANDMINE'S SCENARIO EXECUTED, NOT ARGUED: a full populate_nav_tables rebuild on gaswholesalers.com at 18:16 UTC 2026-07-31 (corr fd85fc84-f021-4e47-801a-db4c90174127) — the DELETE-and-rebuild cycle itself — reproduced all 19 pre-existing nav rows and ADDED 4 /tools/ rows. Zero lost. Pre-flight check reported unreproducible_rows=0.

DIRECTION OF TRAVEL IS THE OPPOSITE OF DELETION: the landmine's own pre-run count query returned 16 child-path nav rows across 7 domains on 2026-07-30; re-run 2026-07-31 it returns 26 across 8 domains (gamesdesign 8, leopardess 5, gaswholesalers 4, robot-hands 2, webdesign 2, idea.uk 2, dartsonline 2, fundamentallyai 1).

REUSE CHECKED BY EXECUTION, not by reading: datahelpers.ExtractNameFromURL('Tools / AI Readiness Quiz') returns ' AI Readiness Quiz' — leading space — because it is URL-typed (no TrimSpace, strips .html/.htm). Reusing it would put a leading space into every affected nav label.

THE ARGUMENT-CHANGE IS PROVABLY UNREAD: navSimplifyLabel's only use of its label parameter is 'if len(label) <= 15 { return label }' (nav_tables.go:575-577); navLabelForPage reaches that call only on the len(label) > 30 branch.

plan.risks: ROUND 3: the rule is now NARROWER than round 2 — only a whitespace-delimited slash is treated as a category separator — which is what stops 'A/B Test Calculator' being mangled to 'B Test Calculator'. Consequence a reviewer should weigh: a label written 'Tools/AI Readiness Quiz' with no spaces is NOT stripped and would keep its slash. No live row uses that form (all 8 use 'Tools / X'), and the alternative was mangling a real name, so the trade is deliberate. The guardian's round-2 point about co-equal separators ('Terms / Privacy' -> 'Privacy') still stands for the whitespace-delimited form and still has no live instance. ROUND 2 ADDITION — independence of this edit from the nav-updater delete landmine, which four seats raised: this changes navLabelForPage, a pure string function on the label, called at INSERT time inside insertNavItem. It touches no classification, no group assignment and no DELETE, so it cannot change WHICH rows exist, only what one column says. Confirmed empirically by running a full rebuild (19 rows reproduced, 4 added, 0 lost). Behavioural surface is 7 flagged pages fleet-wide, of which 2 change from a verbatim slash-bearing label to its last segment and 2 change from a URL-derived label to the planner's better-capitalised words ('Password Entropy' -> 'Password Strength Physics', 'Review Council Simulator' -> 'AI Review Council Simulator'); 3 are unchanged because they remain oversized and still resolve through navSimplifyLabel. A reviewer should check two things. FIRST, the semantic assumption: last-segment is correct for a 'Category / Page' prefix, which is the shape of all 8 live rows, but it would mangle a hypothetical authored label where the slash joins two co-equal words (e.g. 'Terms / Privacy' would become 'Privacy'). No such row exists today; the alternative of rejecting only a leading 'Tools /' was not taken because it hard-codes one category. SECOND, the ordering: the prefix is dropped BEFORE the <=30 test deliberately, so that a long label cannot use the prefix drop to bypass the length guard — if that ordering were reversed, 'Tools / Agent Architecture Complexity Estimator' would render as a 39-character footer item. Nothing here changes which pages appear in nav, only what they are called; page classification, group assignment and ordering are untouched. Not addressed on purpose: the dead pre-A6 twin rerenderSimplifyNavLabel is left in place rather than repaired or deleted, because deleting reachable-looking code is a separate decision from fixing a live label, and its two callers are already annotated DEPRECATED with the sole call site commented out.
